answer: Behavioral fingerprint inlet. Each agent’s continuous interaction trace—timing, phrasing, and decision order—flows through a shared inlet that flags near-identical sequences. A duplicated identity must diverge its trace enough to clear a similarity tide threshold, forcing per-sybil retraining and continuous drift maintenance. Identities also submit one random marble draw per epoch; clones replaying the same draw are linked. The attacker pays ongoing behavioral divergence costs plus lost draw entropy for every extra identity.
